message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Three newly reported vulnerabilities from the last 24 hours were verified as relevant to the primary product scope. All concern exposure to compromised eMudhra certificate-authority keys, but they affect distinct monitored products and are retained as separate findings.

**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined, normalized, and deduplicated. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-23 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-24 23:40 UTC (2026-10-24 05:10 IST through 2026-10-25 05:10 IST).

### CVE-2026-115557: Python `ssl` certificate validation

- **Affected product/component:** Python / CPython `ssl` module
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 4.0 score 9.4
- **Description:** Python added a denylist so TLS certificate chains containing known compromised eMudhra intermediate CA keys are rejected even when certificate revocation is not configured. The official notice does not clearly identify an affected-version range.
- **Why relevant:** Python is explicitly present in the monitored product list.
- **Sources:** [Python Security Announce](https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce%40python.org/message/FNAJMZV6XQYLVPABNINDMF3VF66AYLW4/), [GitHub Advisory Database](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x547-2835-q547)

### CVE-2026-114820: Oracle Java SE JSSE vulnerability

- **Affected product/component:** Oracle Java SE, JSSE
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 3.1 score 9.1
- **Description:** Oracle reports a remotely exploitable, unauthenticated JSSE vulnerability associated with impacted eMudhra root CA certificates. Successful exploitation could compromise confidentiality and integrity; Oracle issued updated Java releases that remove the affected certificates.
- **Why relevant:** Oracle Java is explicitly present in the monitored product list.
- **Source:** [Oracle Security Alert](https://www.oracle.com/security-alerts/alert-cve-2026-114820.html)

### CVE-2026-115929: MongoDB Compass certificate validation

- **Affected product/component:** MongoDB Compass before 1.53.1
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 4.0 score 7.6
- **Description:** Compass relied on an Electron TLS root store containing recoverable eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. Compass 1.53.1 updates Electron to address the issue.
- **Why relevant:** MongoDB is in the monitored list, and Compass is an official MongoDB product identified by the mandatory ecosystem sweep.
- **Sources:** [MongoDB Compass 1.53.1 release](https://github.com/mongodb-js/compass/releases/tag/v1.53.1), [GitHub Advisory Database](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r9qr-cj53-q38x)

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations and libraries, MongoDB notices, CVE/NVD records, GitHub advisories, and CISA sources. No other in-window MongoDB finding was verified.

### Review priority

Immediate review is recommended for Oracle Java SE because of its 9.1 critical rating and unauthenticated network attack path. Python environments and MongoDB Compass installations should also be inventoried promptly; confirm deployed versions and follow the cited vendor guidance.
